text:
alex: quick heads-up — int4 run on candidate-16b showed ~18% token-cost drop but we're seeing a ~2.3% drop in top-1 acceptance on the chat eval set. sharing notes.

maria: can you paste the eval breakdown? is the regression uniform or skewed by prompt length? :thinking:

alex: short summary: overall accept_rate 92.1% -> 89.8%, hallucination flag 1.1% -> 2.9%, avg latency 120ms -> 90ms. sample size n=10k (prod-like, heavily skewed to <128 tokens). full logs: s3://redwood-evals/16b-int4/run-2026-03-18/logs.jsonl

sam: hmm looks like we optimized for short-turn throughput. did we rerun on a long-context slice?

alex: not yet. quick ablation I ran locally: for prompts >512 tokens accept_rate diff is 4.8%. so int4 is worse on longer contexts.

li: what generation settings were used? temp/stop/length can interact with quantization artifacts.

maria: also worth noting: KV cache eviction pattern + int4 packing seems to create small attention numerical noise on long seqs — plausible kernel overflow/scale issue.

eval-bot: automated-report: score_delta: {"accept_rate": -2.3, "hallucination": +1.8, "latency_ms": -30}

alex: proposal / mitigation plan:
- run full ablation on sliced eval sets (short/medium/long)
- test quantized kernel with `--kv-fix=true` (branch kv-fix-2026-03)
- holdback 10% of production traffic to fp16 baseline for 48h
- add a regression alert if accept_rate drops >1.5% over 1h window

sam: quick product Q — what's the user risk if we flip? if we keep 10% holdback, do we still hit cost targets?

alex: rough econ: 10% holdback still yields ~16% net unit-cost improvement (was 18% fully rolled). with fallback-on-failure enabled, expected savings ~12%. detailed calc in sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/UNIT-ECON-16B-INT4

maria: reproducible commands for ablation:
```
python evals/run_ablation.py \
  --model candidate-16b-int4 \
  --slices short,medium,long \
  --n 5000 \
  --metrics accept_rate,hallucination,latency
```

li: ops: if you toggle `--kv-fix` we'll canary on 3 nodes first. I'll open canary cluster and gate rollout behind feature flag `feat/kv-fix`.

alex: canary config I propose:
```
deploy:
  model: candidate-16b-int4
  canary: 3
  holdback: 10%
  fallback: candidate-16b-fp16
  routes: ["chat-prod-us","chat-prod-eu"]
  kernel_flags: ["--kv-fix=true"]
```

sam: product will draft a short GTN note for sales: "Safe progressive rollout: up to 18% token-cost reduction with staged holdback and automatic fallback for quality regressions." will loop in GTN.

maria: next steps (agreed):
1) alex run ablations and post stratified table here (EOD tomorrow)
2) li open canary and prepare feature flag + rollback playbook
3) sam coordinate comms with GTN and support to watch adoption signals

alex: starting ablations now, will publish slice CSVs + p95/p50 deltas in this thread. :rocket:

sam: thx — :thumbsup:
